thread.title: Tech Today: Apple Glow and Gloom, Kodak Soars Again, Micron Worries

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Apple Glow and Gloom, Kodak Soars Again, Micron Worries
text:
CES attendees run for cover amidst a freak rainstorm in Las Vegas on Tuesday. Wednesday, skies were fairly clear. Here are some things going on today in your world of tech :
The skies have cleared over Las Vegas, after a very wet Tuesday, that shocked both locals and visitors to the Consumer Electronics Show .
Weather Dot Com says things should be Sunny through Friday, although one cabbie here told me yesterday it’s going to be wet again on Thursday. Fingers crossed.
Shares of Eastman Kodak ( KODK ) continue to soar today on Tuesday’s blockchain news, rising another 66% to $11.29, after more than doubling yesterday. But keep in mind the words of Kodak CEO Jeff Clarke , who told me in an interview that his company’s introduction of a new currency, Kodak Coins, doesn’t really justify the huge jump in price.
Shares of Apple ( AAPL ) are down $1.04, or 0.6%, at $173.29, as its world continues to be a mix of promise and gloom.
On the gloom side, U.S. Senate Commerce Committee chair John Thune has sent a letter to CEO Tim Cook asking about the recent brouhaha over the battery of the iPhone. He wants data, according to The Hill ’s Ali Breland , about consumer complaints over the slowed-down performance of older iPhones. Also, the Financial Times ’s Vanessa Houlder reports the company is being forced to pay an extra £136 million in the U.K. following a review of the accounts of one of its European subsidiaries. And there’s still chatter going on about that Jana Partners /Calpers demand the company address children’s addiction to the iPhone.
On the positive side, R.W. Baird ’s William Power this morning reiterates an Outperform rating, and a $190 price target, writing that he expects “another strong iPhone cycle” this fall, and the comapny stands to get multiple benefits from tax reform , including another $100 billion potentially added to the company’s buyback efforts from repatriating its overseas cash.
Shares of cloud computing company Workday ( WDAY ) are up $3.96, or 3.6%, at $113.66, after Keith Weiss of Morgan Stanley this morning raised his rating on the shares to Overweight from Equal Weight, and raised his price target to $108 from $145, writing that worries about the company’s rate of increase of its “ billings ” is overblown, that the company has many ways in which it can “sustain strong top-line growth,” and that its “best in class units” are going to lead to expanding profit margins.
The Street is still pondering Micron Technology ’s ( MU ) announcement Monday that its partnership with Intel ( INTC ) to produce NAND flash is going to change after the next model of chips comes out, with the two companies developing diverging, separate roadmaps.
Yesterday, Micron’s CFO Ernie Maddock sounded upbeat about the future of flash during a JP Morgan conference at CES.
Today, Mark Newman of Bernstein writes this is a negative for Micron, as it means the company will take up the part of R&D investment that Intel had been paying, with perhaps up to a 14% hit to operating profit in fiscal 2019 and 2020. It’s also a negative for the industry, he thinks, if it means potential fragmentation of the industry.
"We worry that this opens Intel up to collaborate with Chinese partners in NAND, namely Tsinghua Unigroup, which is desperate to get its hands on proven memory technology,” writes Newman.
Micron stock today is down 70 cents, or 1.7%, at $42.27.
